Szczucin Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Szczucin, Poland

Not demolished. Jews likely settled in Szczucin in the 18th century; Icchak Horowitz, founder of the Szczucin Hasidic dynasty, was associated with the town. By 1921, 491 Jews made up 36% of the population, mostly killed by Germans in 1942. This cemetery, probably established in the 19th century, received reburials in January 1940 of victims shot on September 12, 1939, and originally buried at the church square; Jews caught hiding during the war were also buried here. A 1946-1947 negotiation between the Poviat Jewish Committee and local authorities to trade cemetery fencing for mikveh ownership rights likely fell through amid postwar legal disruption. Poland formally closed the cemetery in 1957.
